summary: SIP is often used to reach services such as voicemail and interactive voice response systems. This document describes a convention for forming SIP service URIs that ask for a particular service when a call is redirected to such an application. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC defines two SIP URI parameters for calls redirected to services such as voicemail. One identifies the mailbox, and the other gives the reason the call was redirected.

questions: sip uri target and cause parameters
how does sip redirect to voicemail
subtitle: SIP URI parameters that tell a voicemail or similar service who to serve and why.

tldr.problem: A voicemail or interactive voice response system needs the mailbox and reason for a redirected call, but systems lacked a shared URI convention for that information.
tldr.mechanism: The Request-URI can carry a target parameter for the mailbox and a cause parameter for the SIP response that caused redirection.
tldr.outcome: The convention depends on the proxy knowing that the application supports it and is updated by RFC 8119.

today: RFC 4458 is an Informational RFC published in April 2006. It is updated by RFC 8119.

sections.title: Information a Voicemail Service Needs
sections.content:
A voicemail or unified messaging system may need to know which mailbox to use and why a call arrived. For example, a system may provide a different greeting when a user is busy than when the user does not answer.

SIP signaling could carry the information, but the RFC says there was no common convention for expressing it. A shared URI convention can help call-control systems, gateways, and messaging systems from different vendors interoperate.
sections.plainLanguage: A voicemail service needs to know whose mailbox should receive a call and what caused the call to be redirected. This RFC gives systems a shared way to include those details.

sections.title: The target and cause Parameters
sections.content:
The SIP Request-URI identifies the voicemail service. Its target parameter identifies the mailbox or redirecting address, and its cause parameter contains the SIP status code that led to retargeting. For example, cause 486 indicates that the user was busy.

Characters in a target value that are not valid as written in a URI must be escaped. The RFC lists status codes for reasons including unknown or unavailable, busy, no reply, and unconditional redirection. If a network has no matching cause, it maps the reason to 302 Unconditional.
sections.plainLanguage: The URI adds a target for the mailbox and a cause for the redirection. A code such as 486 tells the service that the user was busy.

sections.title: Forwarding a Busy Call
sections.content:
In one example, Alice calls Bob and Bob’s proxy receives a 486 Busy Here response. The proxy then sends an INVITE to voicemail with a Request-URI containing Bob’s target and cause 486.

Another example has Bob’s endpoint return a 302 response whose Contact URI carries the same parameters. The RFC also shows a gateway case where the URI identifies both the voicemail system and the subscriber’s mailbox.
sections.plainLanguage: When Bob is busy, the proxy can redirect Alice’s call to voicemail and include Bob’s mailbox and the busy reason in the new request.

sections.title: Limitations, History, and Security
sections.content:
The proxy must be configured to know whether the unified messaging system understands these parameters. The convention also carries only relatively simple redirection information. History-Info can record the original request and later retargeting steps, and can preserve the parameters if a downstream proxy replaces the Request-URI.

The parameters need integrity protection so an attacker cannot redirect a message to the wrong mailbox. The RFC recommends TLS for protecting signaling between the proxy and the messaging system or gateway. Privacy services must remove the target and cause parameters when they perform the specified privacy function.
sections.plainLanguage: The proxy must know that the destination service supports these parameters. Protected signaling helps prevent changes that could send a call to the wrong mailbox.
